meta.project: AI Clinical Scribe Platform — DevOps / CI-CD workstream
meta.purpose: Companion to the repo-root /feature-list.json, NOT a rival source of truth — lives in devops/ specifically so it (and devops/AGENTS.md) only load into context when working in this directory, not on every product-coding session. Tracks containerization, IaC, and CI/CD — a distinct workstream whose priority order doesn't fit the root list's product tiers (Tier 0 airtight-core / Tier 1 differentiators / Tier 2 stretch). Cross-references the root list where relevant: this plan is the concrete path to unblock infra.rds_postgres_private and infra.ec2_nginx_tls, which have sat `blocked` there pending real AWS access.
howToUse: Same discipline as feature-list.json: work top-down by tier, one feature at a time.
Do NOT start a Tier 1 item until every Tier 0 item is 'passing' — Tier 0 is the security/auth foundation everything else authenticates through.

Every acceptance criterion has a real, runnable verification command in `verify` — a feature moves to 'passing' only when that command actually succeeds, not when it 'looks right'. Record the command's output as evidence in progress.md.

Branch + PR per feature, same as the root list (see devops/AGENTS.md workflow rules). Infra changes additionally require a `terraform plan` posted in the PR before merge (see devops.ci_terraform_plan).

statusLegend.failing: Not yet implemented, or verify command doesn't pass. Initial state for everything.
statusLegend.passing: verify command succeeds against the real target (real AWS, not a mock).
statusLegend.blocked: Cannot proceed until a dependency (usually AWS account access) is resolved.

tiers.0: FOUNDATION. Containerization + IaC bootstrap + federated auth + registries. Nothing in Tier 1/2 can run without this — no static AWS keys anywhere, ever.
tiers.1: CI GATES. Every PR must pass these before merge is even possible: secret scan, image build, vulnerability scan. Gate quality, not yet touching real infra.
tiers.2: CD PIPELINES. Push-on-main, deploy-on-main, rollback, and manual multi-env dispatch. Depends on Tier 0 (auth/registry) + Tier 1 (gates) being green.
tiers.3: HARDENING. Stretch — automatic rollback on failed health check, Terraform plan-on-PR. Only after Tier 0-2 are solid.

meta.architectureDecision: Docker Compose on EC2 (NOT ECS/Fargate) — chosen over a container-orchestrator migration because docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:54 and infra/DEPLOY.md already commit to EC2+nginx specifically for nginx's `proxy_buffering off` behavior, which scribe.generate_stream's SSE streaming (already `passing` in feature-list.json) depends on. An ALB in front of ECS would need that streaming behavior re-verified for no real benefit. Deploys/rollbacks run over AWS SSM Run Command (IAM-scoped, no SSH keys/bastion) rather than a container scheduler's rolling-update primitive.
meta.environments: dev / staging / prod, each its own EC2 instance + own RDS instance, provisioned via one parameterized Terraform module (workspaces/tfvars per env) rather than 3 duplicated feature entries — the acceptance criteria and verify commands are identical per environment.
meta.invariantsRef: AGENTS.md §2 still applies in full — especially [SECRETS] (no static AWS keys, ever — see devops.terraform_oidc_github) and [RDS-PRIVATE].

features.title: Production Dockerfile for apps/api
features.description: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the NestJS API: build stage compiles TS, final stage is a slim runtime image, non-root user, base image pinned by digest (not a floating tag).
acceptance: Multi-stage build — final image contains no dev dependencies, no TS source, no build tooling.
Base image pinned by sha256 digest, not `:latest` or a bare version tag.
Runs as a non-root user.
Image responds on GET /health once started.
verify: docker build -t scribe-api:local -f apps/api/Dockerfile .
docker run -d --rm --name scribe-api-smoke -p 3099:3000 --env-file apps/api/.env.example -e AI_PROVIDER=mock scribe-api:local
curl -f http://localhost:3099/health && docker exec scribe-api-smoke whoami | grep -v root
docker stop scribe-api-smoke

features.title: Production Dockerfile for apps/web
features.description: Multi-stage Dockerfile for the Vite/React app: build stage runs `vite build`, final stage serves the static bundle via a slim nginx image, non-root, digest-pinned.
acceptance: Multi-stage build — final image is nginx serving only the built dist/, no node_modules or source.
Base image pinned by sha256 digest.
Runs as non-root (nginx-unprivileged or equivalent).
Serves index.html and proxies /api/* per infra/nginx.conf's existing rewrite rule.

docker run -d --rm --name scribe-web-smoke -p 8099:8080 scribe-web:local

features.title: Terraform remote state backend
features.description: S3 bucket (versioned, encrypted) + DynamoDB lock table for Terraform state, bootstrapped once outside the main Terraform config to avoid a chicken-and-egg problem. Local state never committed.
acceptance: State bucket has versioning + SSE enabled, blocks public access.
Lock table prevents concurrent apply (verified by a deliberate second `terraform apply` while one is in-flight).
`terraform init` in infra/terraform/ succeeds against the remote backend with no local .tfstate created.
verify: cd infra/terraform && terraform init
terraform state list  # reachable, non-error even if empty
aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket <state-bucket> | grep -q Enabled

features.title: GitHub Actions federated AWS auth (OIDC, no static keys)
features.description: IAM OIDC identity provider trusting token.actions.githubusercontent.com, plus an IAM role GitHub Actions assumes via aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials. Trust policy scoped to this repo and specific ref patterns (main, pull_request) — not org-wide. Policy is least-privilege: ecr:*  scoped to the two repos, ssm:SendCommand scoped to the deploy tag, no wildcard admin.
acceptance: No AWS access key / secret key exists anywhere in GitHub secrets or the codebase — auth is 100% OIDC (AGENTS.md [SECRETS]).
Trust policy's `token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub` condition is scoped to this specific repo, not `repo:*`.
Role policy denies anything outside {ECR push to the 2 named repos, SSM SendCommand to deploy-tagged instances, ECS/EC2 describe for smoke checks} — no `*` resource on a mutating action.
verify: gh workflow run oidc-smoke-test.yml && gh run watch
# In the workflow: aws sts get-caller-identity must print the expected role ARN with no AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID env var set anywhere in the job
aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn <role-arn> --action-names ecr:PutImage --resource-arns 'arn:aws:ecr:*:*:repository/unrelated-repo' | grep -q implicitDeny
features.rubric: DevOps: federated auth, zero static credentials. Passing 2026-08-18: OIDC provider + scribe-github-actions-deploy role + least-privilege policy all real and live in AWS. Full oidc-smoke-test.yml GitHub Actions run succeeded end-to-end via a real pull_request trigger (PR #10): role assumed via OIDC with zero static keys, temporary STS credentials confirmed (ASIA-prefixed + session token), in-scope ECR/SSM actions succeeded, out-of-scope ECR repo and iam:ListUsers both genuinely denied by AWS. simulate-principal-policy also confirmed least-privilege scoping directly. Three real bugs found and fixed along the way (see devops/progress.md): a YAML syntax error that silently failed every run since the workflow's creation, an OIDC trust policy mismatched against GitHub's actual immutable-ID subject-claim format for this repo, and a credential-check logic bug that conflated env-var presence with static-key usage.

features.title: ECR repositories (api + web) with immutable tags
features.description: Terraform-provisioned ECR repos for scribe-api and scribe-web. Tag immutability ON (a pushed tag can never be overwritten — this is what makes 'use the SHA, never latest' actually enforceable, not just a convention). Native ECR scan-on-push enabled as defense-in-depth alongside the Trivy CI gate. Lifecycle policy expires untagged images after 7 days.
acceptance: Both repos have imageTagMutability = IMMUTABLE.
scanOnPush enabled on both.
Lifecycle policy expires untagged manifests >7 days old.
Pushing the same tag twice fails (proves immutability, not just configured).
verify: aws ecr describe-repositories --repository-names scribe-api scribe-web --query 'repositories[].imageTagMutability' | grep -c IMMUTABLE  # expect 2
docker push <account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/scribe-api:smoke-test-tag  # first push succeeds
docker push <account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/scribe-api:smoke-test-tag  # second push to same tag must be REJECTED
features.rubric: DevOps: registry, immutable artifacts. Reconciled to passing 2026-08-18 (status-reconciliation sprint; original 2026-08-18 blocked note is now stale — a later session on the same feature branch (origin/feat/devops-terraform-ecr, commit be8a00f) actually cleared the ecr:TagResource gap plus a second ecr:GetLifecyclePolicy gap and got this fully passing, but that doc-flip commit was never merged to main, so feature-list.json kept reading blocked while real AWS state and the branch's own docs already said passing — this entry re-verifies that independently against live AWS rather than trusting either doc). All 4 acceptance criteria confirmed for real this session with AWS_PROFILE=devops-agent: (1) `aws ecr describe-repositories --repository-names scribe-api scribe-web` → both imageTagMutability=IMMUTABLE; (2) both imageScanningConfiguration.scanOnPush=true; (3) `aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy` on both → rule expiring untagged images sinceImagePushed>7 days; (4) live double-push test: pushed alpine:3.19 to scribe-api:smoke-test-tag (already present from a prior session, re-push of identical digest succeeded as expected/idempotent), then pushed a genuinely different image (alpine:3.18) to the same tag — rejected by ECR: \"The image tag 'smoke-test-tag' already exists in the 'scribe-api' repository and cannot be overwritten because the tag is immutable.\" `terraform plan` in infra/terraform/ (AWS_PROFILE=devops-agent, plan-only, no apply run) shows zero drift (\"No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.\") — both aws_ecr_repository and aws_ecr_lifecycle_policy resources are tracked in real remote state, refuting the old rubric's \"no partial resources created\" as no longer the current reality. Provenance: both repos + lifecycle policies were created via local `terraform apply` under AWS_PROFILE=devops-agent (git history shows commit 8a35335 on feat/devops-terraform-ecr, merged to main as PR #11) — not via CI, since no GitHub Actions workflow in this repo runs `terraform apply` at all yet (only secret-scan/build-images/oidc-smoke-test exist). This matches the same documented Tier-0-bootstrap local-apply exception already used for devops.terraform_backend and devops.terraform_oidc_github (chicken-and-egg: the CD/OIDC apply pipeline that would let this run from CI doesn't exist until later Tier 2 work), not an undocumented workaround. Known gap unchanged: devops-agent still lacks ecr:BatchDeleteImage (reconfirmed live, AccessDeniedException) — the smoke-test-tag image (now alpine:3.19's digest) remains in scribe-api, harmless leftover, not worth a dedicated IAM round.

features.title: Terraform: VPC + private RDS (unblocks infra.rds_postgres_private)
features.description: VPC with private subnets for RDS, public/private split for the EC2 instances. RDS Postgres + pgvector, no public IP, SG accepts 5432 only from the compute SG. This is the real-AWS execution of feature-list.json's infra.rds_postgres_private, which has sat blocked on account access — flip that item to passing once this runs for real, don't duplicate its acceptance criteria here.
acceptance: RDS has PubliclyAccessible = false.
RDS security group's only inbound rule is 5432 from the EC2 security group (source = SG reference, not a CIDR).
A connection attempt from outside the VPC times out / is refused.
pgvector extension enabled post-provision.
verify: aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier scribe-prod --query 'DBInstances[0].PubliclyAccessible'  # expect false
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c 'SELECT 1' # from OUTSIDE the VPC — must fail/timeout
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -c "SELECT * FROM pg_extension WHERE extname='vector'" # from inside — must return a row
features.rubric: DevOps: IaC — networking + database. 2026-08-19: REAL AWS applied — one shared VPC (10.30.0.0/16) + per-env (dev/staging/prod) public+private subnet pairs (2 AZs) + reserved compute SGs + RDS SGs + 3 real db.t4g.micro Postgres-16 RDS instances (scribe-dev/scribe-staging/scribe-prod), all via `infra/terraform/main.tf` for_each, single state, applied locally (AWS_PROFILE=devops-agent) per this workstream's established Tier-0-bootstrap local-apply precedent. Criteria 1-3 FULLY VERIFIED for real, for all 3 envs: (1) `aws rds describe-db-instances` -> PubliclyAccessible=false x3, status=available x3; (2) `aws ec2 describe-security-groups` on all 3 RDS SGs -> single ingress rule, tcp/5432, source=UserIdGroupPairs (compute SG reference) only, IpRanges=[] on all 3 -- confirmed zero CIDR-based ingress; (3) real `docker run postgres:16 psql "postgresql://...scribe-dev...?connect_timeout=5"` from this machine (outside the VPC) -> `psql: error: connection ... failed: timeout expired` against the real private IP (10.30.11.148) -- genuine timeout, not a mock. Criterion 4 (pgvector, from inside the VPC) NOT proven this session: built the full throwaway-EC2 SSM-probe mechanism (option (a) from the dispatch brief -- AL2023 instance, SSM-only, no SSH, IAM role w/ only AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, attached to all 3 envs' compute SGs, created/torn down via raw AWS CLI, kept OUT of Terraform state) but `ssm:SendCommand` on the AWS-owned `AWS-RunShellScript` document was denied for devops-agent -- a real, new, minimal IAM gap (devops-agent's `SsmDeploy` statement's tag-based condition can never match the document resource, since AWS-owned documents can't carry a `deploy` tag; the fix mirrors a pattern this repo's own OIDC role policy already gets right -- see devops/manual.md Step 10, Gap C, for the exact 1-statement fix). Probe instance + its IAM role/profile terminated/deleted immediately after the failure, nothing left running. Two OTHER real gaps hit and self-serve-avoided (not blocking, but disclosed -- see devops/manual.md Step 10 Gaps A/B): `ec2:ModifySubnetAttribute` not granted (avoided by dropping `map_public_ip_on_launch` from public subnets -- EC2 can request a public IP per-instance instead, next feature); KMS access for `manage_master_user_password` not granted (avoided by switching the RDS master password to a Terraform-generated `random_password`, a disclosed downgrade from 'password never touches Terraform state' to 'password lives only in the encrypted, versioned, gitignored remote S3 state' -- swap back once Gap B's KMS grant lands). Status left `blocked` (not `passing`) honestly: 3 of 4 acceptance criteria proven, but the feature's own literal 4th verify command (pgvector from inside) is unrun. `infra.rds_postgres_private` in the ROOT repo's feature-list.json is now unblockable in the sense that real, live, correctly-firewalled RDS instances exist -- but the human running that flip should know criterion 4 is the one open item. Terraform plan is 100% clean (`No changes. Your infrastructure matches the configuration.`) after all fixes. Cost: ~$37-40/mo for the 3 RDS instances (db.t4g.micro + 20GB gp3 each, no NAT gateways used) -- see devops/sprint-contract.md for the full breakdown. Next: devops.terraform_compute_envs (EC2/nginx/TLS, same 3 envs) can proceed in parallel/next -- its own throwaway-probe-adjacent SSM needs will likely hit the same Gap C, so getting that one IAM grant first would unblock both this feature's remaining criterion AND de-risk the next feature's own SSM-based deploy mechanism. RE-ATTEMPTED 2026-08-19 (second pass, same day): a human reported applying devops/manual.md Step 10 Gap C's exact minimal IAM fix via a newly-set-up scoped grantor role (assumed via their own low-privilege user + MFA, not root). Re-verified independently rather than trusted -- git-fetched/checked out this exact branch, confirmed `terraform plan` (AWS_PROFILE=devops-agent) showed zero drift before touching anything, reconfirmed criteria 1-2 still hold for all 3 envs (PubliclyAccessible=false x3; RDS SGs still single-rule/SG-reference-only/zero-CIDR x3). Built a FRESH throwaway SSM-only EC2 probe from scratch (same design as before: Amazon Linux 2023, no SSH/key pair, IAM role scoped to only AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore, attached to all 3 envs' compute SGs), confirmed it reached `running` state with a real public IP and the correct instance profile. `aws ssm send-command --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --instance-ids <probe-id> ...` FAILED with the exact same AccessDeniedException as the original attempt, word-for-word: `... not authorized to perform: ssm:SendCommand on resource: arn:aws:ssm:us-east-1::document/AWS-RunShellScript because no identity-based policy allows the ssm:SendCommand action`. The fix has NOT landed -- criterion 4 remains unproven. Also newly observed: `ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation` (used to poll SSM registration) is ALSO denied for devops-agent even against an instance tagged `deploy=true`, a related but distinct gap (no single taggable resource in that list-type call for the SsmDeploy statement's condition to match against) -- documented in devops/manual.md Step 10's new subsection, not blocking (SendCommand was tested directly) but worth folding into any future grant. Probe instance terminated and its IAM role/instance profile deleted immediately after the denial -- confirmed via `aws iam get-role`/`get-instance-profile` both returning NoSuchEntity, `aws ec2 describe-instances` confirming `terminated` state. Status remains `blocked`, honestly -- still 3 of 4 criteria proven, criterion 4 re-attempted and still genuinely blocked on the same IAM gap. Full evidence: devops/manual.md Step 10's 'RE-ATTEMPTED 2026-08-19' subsection, devops/progress.md's second 2026-08-19 entry.

features.title: Terraform: EC2 + nginx + TLS per environment, dev/staging/prod (unblocks infra.ec2_nginx_tls)
features.description: One parameterized Terraform module (workspace or tfvars per environment) provisioning an EC2 instance running Docker Compose (api container + nginx container, TLS via certbot or ACM-issued cert on an attached ALB-free nginx), for each of dev/staging/prod. IAM instance role scoped to Secrets Manager (that env's secret only) + SSM (to receive deploy commands) — no long-lived keys on disk. This is the real-AWS execution of feature-list.json's infra.ec2_nginx_tls.
acceptance: 3 environments provisioned (dev, staging, prod), each its own EC2 instance + SG (80/443 only) + IAM instance profile.
Node process never directly exposed on 80/443 — nginx container terminates TLS and proxies to the api container on a private Docker network.

nginx config carries forward `proxy_buffering off` / `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for the SSE generation endpoint (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:28) — a regression here silently breaks scribe.generate_stream's streaming.
Cert is CA-issued (Let's Encrypt via certbot), not self-signed.
Instance is reachable via SSM Session Manager, not open SSH (port 22 closed in the SG).
verify: for env in dev staging prod; do terraform workspace select $env && terraform apply -auto-approve; done
curl -sI https://<env>.scribe.example.com | grep -q 'HTTP/2 200'

openssl s_client -connect <env>.scribe.example.com:443 -servername <env>.scribe.example.com </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -issuer | grep -v 'CN = <env>.scribe.example.com'  # not self-signed
curl -N https://<env>.scribe.example.com/api/encounters/<id>/scribe/generate ... | ts '%.s'  # confirm chunks arrive over time, not buffered as one blob
nmap -p 22 <env-ec2-public-ip>  # expect closed/filtered, not open
features.rubric: DevOps: IaC — compute + TLS + SSE-safety regression check. Blocked on real AWS account access, same as infra.ec2_nginx_tls in feature-list.json.

features.title: CI: hardcoded-secret scan as a required PR check
features.description: Promotes the existing scripts/check-no-committed-secrets.sh (gitleaks, currently a local/manual script backing infra.env_secrets) into an actual required GitHub Actions check on every PR — not just something an agent is supposed to remember to run.
acceptance: gitleaks (or equivalent) runs on every PR via GitHub Actions.
The check is a required status check — a PR cannot merge while it's red, enforced by branch protection.
A PR containing a deliberately fake AWS-shaped key string fails the check.
verify: git checkout -b test/secret-scan-smoke && echo 'AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP' >> scratch.txt && git commit -am test && git push
gh pr create --fill && gh pr checks  # secret-scan job must show failure
gh api repos/:owner/:repo/branches/main/protection | jq '.required_status_checks.contexts' | grep -q secret-scan

features.title: CI: build both images on every PR (not pushed)
features.description: GitHub Actions builds scribe-api and scribe-web via Docker Buildx on every PR, with layer caching, purely to validate the Dockerfiles compile — nothing is pushed to a registry from a PR build.
acceptance: Both images build successfully on every PR.
Build uses layer caching (GHA cache backend) so PR builds aren't full-cold every time.
No push step runs on a PR — push only happens from devops.cd_push_ecr_main, on main.
verify: gh pr checks  # build-api and build-web jobs both green
gh run view <run-id> --log | grep -qv 'docker push'  # confirm no push happened on a PR run

Passing 2026-08-18: workflow merged (PR #14) before the implementing agent finished its own verify/status-flip step (it was still waiting on its own PR's CI run when the PR got merged) — independently re-verified after the fact directly against the merged run: `gh pr checks 14` showed both `build-api`/`build-web` green, `gh run view --log` on the run confirmed zero `docker push` invocations, and the workflow file confirms `push: false`/`load: false` plus `cache-from`/`cache-to: type=gha` on both jobs.

features.title: CI: Trivy vulnerability scan on both built images
features.description: Trivy scans both PR-built images for CRITICAL/HIGH CVEs. Job fails the PR if any are found, with an explicit, reviewed allowlist mechanism (a .trivyignore entry requires a comment linking to why it's accepted) for genuine false positives — not a blanket suppression.
acceptance: Trivy runs against both images on every PR, after devops.ci_build_images.
Job fails on any CRITICAL or HIGH severity finding not explicitly allowlisted.
A PR built from a deliberately outdated/vulnerable base image fails the check; the real Dockerfiles pass.
verify: trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL,HIGH --ignorefile .trivyignore scribe-api:local  # expect exit 0 on the real Dockerfile
docker build -t scribe-api:vuln-test -f - . <<< 'FROM node:18.0.0'  # ancient base
trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL,HIGH scribe-api:vuln-test  # expect non-zero exit
features.rubric: DevOps: CI security gate — image vulnerabilities. Passing 2026-08-18: real `trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH scribe-api:local` initially found 66 real findings (22 unfixable Debian OS pkgs, 19 leaked devDependencies incl. vite/vitest/esbuild, 25 in npm CLI's own vendored deps) plus scribe-web:local was already clean (0 findings). Root-caused and fixed for real, not suppressed: (1) apps/api/Dockerfile's `pnpm install --prod` didn't actually prune devDependencies already on disk (a real bug) — added `pnpm prune --prod`, which does, eliminating vite/vitest/esbuild + their CVEs; (2) removed the bundled npm CLI from the runtime stage (image only ever runs `node`, never npm/npx) — eliminated CVEs in npm's own vendored tar/sigstore/ip-address/brace-expansion/picomatch; (3) pnpm-workspace.yaml `overrides` bump multer >=2.2.0 / lodash >=4.18.0 (real transitive prod deps via @nestjs/platform-express / @nestjs/config) to patched versions. Confirmed `node:22-slim`'s pinned digest is already the current latest (no newer digest to bump to). Remaining 13 CVE IDs / 22 findings are Debian OS packages with no fix available upstream (Debian status affected/fix_deferred/will_not_fix) and never invoked by this image's runtime (`CMD node apps/api/dist/main.js` only) — allowlisted in root .trivyignore, each with its own justification comment. All three literal verify commands run for real and green: `trivy ... --ignorefile .trivyignore scribe-api:local` exit 0, same for scribe-web:local; `docker build FROM node:18.0.0` + `trivy image` on it exits 1 with 62 CRITICAL + 63 HIGH real findings. Both images re-smoke-tested after the Dockerfile fix (build succeeds, /health OK, non-root `node`/`nginx`) to confirm devops.dockerfile_api/devops.dockerfile_web acceptance still holds. build-images.yml extended (load: true + Trivy CLI install + scan step, same job as the build) rather than a new workflow. `actionlint` clean.

features.title: CD: push SHA-tagged images to ECR on merge to main
features.description: On merge to main only (never on a PR build), after devops.ci_secret_scan + devops.ci_image_scan_trivy are both green: authenticate to AWS via OIDC (devops.terraform_oidc_github), build, tag with the immutable git SHA, push to ECR (devops.terraform_ecr). `latest` is never used as a tag anywhere in this pipeline.
acceptance: Push only triggers on push-to-main, gated on the secret-scan and image-scan jobs having passed for that commit.
Image tag is the git SHA (short or full) — grep the whole workflow file, `latest` must not appear as a tag value.
Auth uses the OIDC role, zero AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/SECRET anywhere in the job.
verify: git log -1 --format=%H  # note the SHA
aws ecr describe-images --repository-name scribe-api --image-ids imageTag=<sha>  # succeeds
aws ecr list-images --repository-name scribe-api --query 'imageIds[].imageTag' | grep -v latest  # 'latest' must not appear
features.rubric: DevOps: CD — immutable artifact publishing. Passing 2026-08-18: `.github/workflows/build-images.yml` extended with a `push: branches: [main]` trigger, a push-only `secret-scan-main` job, and two push-only `push-api`/`push-web` jobs (each `needs: [secret-scan-main, build-*]` with an explicit success-checking `if:`), authenticating via `aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials` to role `scribe-github-actions-deploy` (OIDC only, zero static keys) and pushing `${{ github.sha }}`-tagged images (never `latest`) via `aws-actions/amazon-ecr-login` + `docker/build-push-action`. PR #19 merged to `main` by the human owner (not self-merged); the FIRST real push-to-main run (merge commit `9bba1f2c2920fdd9908d2b1d1207854441037717`) went fully green end-to-end: `secret-scan-main` (success, 10s) -> `build-api`/`build-web` (success, ~1.5min each, includes the Trivy image-scan gate) -> `push-api`/`push-web` (success). All three literal `verify` commands then run for real against that exact merge SHA: `aws ecr describe-images --repository-name scribe-api --image-ids imageTag=9bba1f2c2920fdd9908d2b1d1207854441037717` succeeded (real `imagePushedAt`, real size); same for `scribe-web`; `aws ecr list-images --repository-name scribe-api --query 'imageIds[].imageTag'` returned only `smoke-test-tag`, the real merge SHA, and a leftover manual dry-run tag from pre-merge verification — zero `latest`; same clean result for `scribe-web` (only the merge SHA tag present). Auth confirmed OIDC-only: grep of the whole workflow file shows zero `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`/`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, and a pre-merge real read of the live IAM role policy (`aws iam get-role-policy`) confirmed it grants exactly the ECR push actions used, scoped to scribe-api/scribe-web. PR-triggered checks (this feature's own PR #19) separately confirmed `secret-scan-main`/`push-api`/`push-web` correctly skip on a PR event and never fire outside push-to-main.

features.title: CD: auto-deploy to production on main, via SSM
features.description: After devops.cd_push_ecr_main succeeds, GitHub Actions sends an SSM RunCommand to the prod EC2 instance: pull the new SHA-tagged image, `docker compose up -d --no-deps api`, then a post-deploy smoke test hits /health and a real SSE generate call to confirm streaming still works before declaring success.
acceptance: Deploy triggers automatically after a successful ECR push from main — no manual step.
Deploy runs over SSM RunCommand, not SSH.
Post-deploy smoke test checks /health AND that scribe.generate_stream still yields multiple chunks over time (regression guard for the nginx buffering concern).
A failed smoke test fails the workflow run visibly (does not silently report success).
verify: gh run list --workflow=deploy-prod.yml --limit 1  # latest run status
aws ssm list-command-invocations --command-id <id> --details | jq '.CommandInvocations[0].Status'  # Success
curl -f https://prod.scribe.example.com/health
curl -N https://prod.scribe.example.com/api/encounters/<id>/scribe/generate ... | ts '%.s'  # multiple timestamped chunks, not one blob
features.rubric: DevOps: CD — automated production deploy with a real smoke test, not a self-report

features.title: CD: rollback workflow to a previous or specific image tag
features.description: A separate workflow_dispatch workflow (not the main-branch push pipeline) taking an `image_tag` input (defaults to the previous successfully-deployed SHA, read from a small deploy-history record written by devops.cd_deploy_prod_on_main). Re-points the target environment's containers to that tag via the same SSM mechanism — no rebuild.
acceptance: Triggerable via `gh workflow run rollback.yml -f environment=prod -f image_tag=<sha>` with no code change required.
Defaults to 'previous successful deploy' when image_tag is omitted, read from recorded deploy history (not guessed).
Same post-deploy smoke test as devops.cd_deploy_prod_on_main runs after rollback.
verify: gh workflow run rollback.yml -f environment=prod -f image_tag=<older-sha>
gh run watch
aws ssm list-command-invocations --command-id <id> | jq '.CommandInvocations[0].Status'  # Success
curl -f https://prod.scribe.example.com/health
features.rubric: DevOps: CD — rollback without a rebuild

features.title: CD: manual multi-environment dispatch (dev/staging/prod)
features.description: A workflow_dispatch workflow with `environment` (dev/staging/prod) and `image_tag` inputs, deploying a specified already-built image to a specified environment outside the main-merge path — e.g. deploying a feature-branch build to staging for review, or re-deploying an old tag to dev. Production runs through this path additionally require a GitHub Environment protection rule (manual approval), since it bypasses the CI-gated main-branch flow.
acceptance: One workflow, parameterized by environment + image_tag, targets the correct environment's EC2 instance via SSM (never cross-deploys to the wrong env).
dev and staging deploy immediately on dispatch.
prod additionally requires a manual approval (GitHub Environments protection rule) before the SSM command fires — verify by confirming the run pauses in 'Waiting' state.
Deploying a tag that was never pushed to ECR fails cleanly with a clear error, not a silent no-op.
verify: gh workflow run manual-deploy.yml -f environment=dev -f image_tag=<sha> && gh run watch  # deploys immediately
gh workflow run manual-deploy.yml -f environment=prod -f image_tag=<sha>; gh run view <run-id>  # status shows 'waiting' pending approval
gh workflow run manual-deploy.yml -f environment=dev -f image_tag=does-not-exist; gh run view <run-id> --log | grep -qi 'not found'
features.rubric: DevOps: CD — manual multi-environment dispatch with a real approval gate on prod

features.title: Stretch: automatic rollback on failed post-deploy health check
features.description: If devops.cd_deploy_prod_on_main's post-deploy smoke test fails, automatically trigger devops.cd_rollback to the previous known-good tag instead of just failing the workflow and leaving prod broken.
acceptance: A deliberately broken deploy (e.g. a build that fails /health) triggers an automatic rollback within N minutes, no human action required.
The auto-rollback is itself logged/notified (not silent) so a human knows it happened.
verify: # deploy a deliberately broken image tag to a test environment
gh workflow run deploy-prod.yml -f image_tag=<broken-sha>
gh run watch  # expect: smoke test fails -> rollback job triggers automatically -> environment ends healthy on the prior tag
curl -f https://<env>.scribe.example.com/health  # healthy again post-auto-rollback

features.title: Stretch: terraform plan posted on infra PRs, apply only on merge
features.description: Any PR touching infra/terraform/** runs `terraform plan` in CI and posts the plan output as a PR comment for human review. `terraform apply` only ever runs from a GitHub Actions job on merge to main, never from a local machine.
acceptance: A PR changing a .tf file gets an automatic plan-output comment.
No `terraform apply` credentials/capability exist outside the main-branch CI job.
A PR that doesn't touch infra/terraform/** does not trigger a plan run (path-filtered).
verify: gh pr create --fill  # on a branch with a .tf change
gh pr view --json comments | jq '.comments[].body' | grep -q 'Terraform Plan'
git diff --name-only main -- infra/terraform/  # sanity check the trigger path filter matches what changed
